title: Dispatch: 19.3.1 repair after Sol S1-S2 (attempt 2)
description: Repair PR #649 per Sol review eshyra-o9bd.19.3.1.2 (read S1 and S2 in full). S1: add the printed visibility predicate to Iron Flask and Sculpt Spells through their compiler inputs (magicItemResidualCombatEffects.ts / mechanicsProjections.ts), following how the other members of the visibility cohort carry it (Eyes of Charming requiresMutualSight; others keep sight in target/activation fields); regenerate; re-inspect the whole non-creature target population for equivalent losses; correct the targeting-qualifiers (F-35) registry reasoning to the true result; add one generalized predicate over the reviewed visibility cohort ('can see' wording -> a sight qualifier in the projection) plus the two exact source cases. S2: extend the O5 non-option-prose invariant to mechanics.effects (each parent effect must be derivable from non-option prose), keeping legitimate parent effects (Dragon Ancestor expertise) and option-keyed procedures valid; demonstrate both source-backed bad states (Hunter's Prey extraDamage 1d8; Superior Hunter's Defense evasion + damageReduction) are rejected (temporary in-memory or reverted mutation; record the demonstration in notes). Diff records.json: only Iron Flask and Sculpt Spells (and any equivalent loss you find and justify) may change. Importer protocol; regenerate pack + inventory; verify:dnd5e-srd-pack; host-memory wait; verify:worktree then commit with &&; notes; close this bead. No push/PR.
notes:
REPAIR of Sol S1-S2 (PR #649 head dc1fca6e), commit dbe6b8d0 on eshyra-o9bd.19.3.1.3.

S1 (visibility): magic-item:iron-flask trap target -> "creature native to another plane of existence that you can see" + requiresSight:true (source p.228 "targeting a creature that you can see within 60 feet"). feature:school-of-evocation:sculpt-spells autoSucceedSave gains requiresSight:true from "other creatures that you can see" (p.54), emitted by a source-regex guard in mechanicsProjections.ts. autoSucceedSave schema admits optBool requiresSight.
- Cohort: non-creature records with a projected target field and sight wording in their own text: 9 (matches Sol). Before: Sculpt and Iron Flask lacked any sight qualifier; the other seven kept it (eyes-of-charming requiresMutualSight; gem, ring of the ram, robe, rod, rope, wand via target strings). After: all nine carry it.
- Re-inspection beyond the cohort (broader sight wording: see/visible/sight/unseen/seen): no further sight loss found (dust of disappearance, potions and philter use "invisible"/"self" without a source sight restriction).
- Registry F-35 statusReasoning corrected: names the two losses, their repair, and the cohort invariant; non-sight qualifiers stated as token-audit only, not per-record proof.
- Generalized predicate: alternativeOptionProjections.test.ts "S1" block pins the 9-record cohort and asserts projectsSight for each; negative control strips the Iron Flask qualifier and the predicate reports false.
- Existing exact expectation srdFeatureMechanics.test.ts Sculpt Spells updated to include requiresSight:true (strengthens, same claim).

S2 (O5 invariant): the invariant now checks mechanics.effects too. Witnesses (fail-closed for unknown kinds): expertise /proficiency bonus is doubled/; saveDcFormula /\bsave dc\b/; proficiency /\bproficien/; healing /\bhit points\b/; abilityCheckModifier /\badvantage\b|\bcheck\b/; extraDamage: the dice literal must appear; evasion /\bevasion\b/; damageReduction /\bhalf\b|\bhalve\b/. Body = description + printed sections with each option's name and text removed. Option-keyed fighter procedures are not parent effects and are unaffected. Dragon Ancestor expertise stays valid (prose witness).

S2 BAD-STATE DEMONSTRATION (negative controls, in memory, in the committed test file):
- Restored Hunter's Prey parent effects [{kind:extraDamage, dice:'1d8'}] -> parentProjectionViolations = ['effects[0] extraDamage 1d8']. Test "rejects the source-backed option-only effects..." passes.
- Restored Superior Hunter's Defense parent saves [{ability:dexterity}] + effects [evasion, damageReduction 0.5] -> violations include 'effects[0] evasion' and 'effects[1] damageReduction 0.5' (plus the save). Same test passes.
- The prior (pre-repair) invariant checked only spellGrants/conditions/saves and so could not see either effect; it is the blind spot Sol identified.

RECORDS CHANGED vs the 19.3.1 head: exactly feature:school-of-evocation:sculpt-spells and magic-item:iron-flask (2 of 1799). No other churn.
